resources.string: VPN authorization was cancelled or denied.
Camera access was denied. You can enable it in system settings or paste the subscription URL.
Camera unavailable. Close the scanner and try again.
This QR code does not contain a valid HTTP or HTTPS subscription URL.
Choose the TCP/IP implementation used by the built-in mihomo TUN: system, gVisor, or mixed.
Keep gVisor by default. Use system to process TCP and UDP with the system stack, or mixed for system TCP and gVisor UDP.
Android always uses the system-authorized VPN/TUN. This changes its stack, not the VPN permission. Saved changes require stopping and starting the connection.
Use an emoji rendered by the device font, or an HTTP/HTTPS image as the subscription icon.
Type an emoji, select one from the grid, or paste an image URL. Detection checks favicon.ico, favicon.png, sub.ico and sub.png at the subscription origin.

An empty icon is detected when importing a URL. Detection sends no subscription query or credentials and stays on the same origin. Images are cached privately; failure uses the globe icon and does not prevent import.
Read a subscription URL from a QR code with the camera.
Tap the scanner beside the URL field and grant camera access. A valid HTTP/HTTPS result fills the field for review.

Recognition runs on this device without Google Play services. Camera frames are neither saved nor uploaded. Scanning does not import or open the URL; closing or backgrounding the scanner releases the camera.
Review system VPN, notification and camera authorization.
VPN consent is requested when connecting. Android 13 or later requests notification permission on first connection. Camera access is requested only when scanning.

Denying notifications does not prevent VPN, but its notification may be hidden. Denying camera access still allows pasted URLs and text. Revoking VPN closes the tunnel and core; no root, storage or battery exemption is required.
